Drive it with `tools/proof/mcp.py` (`mcp.MCP("<dir>/agent.sock")`, `client.call_with(tool, {...})` answers a dict) and the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`, `perform_menu_item` with a `path` list, `play_preview`, `select_inspector_tab`, `assistant_send`, `assistant_answer` and the rest in the root CLAUDE.md). `docs-bugs/loop_live.py` and `loop_live2.py` are a worked example. Make a real test project with `tools/proof/media/`, and generate other media you need (an AVIF, a Latin-1 SRT) into your scratch folder. Stop the instance by the pid the launcher printed. `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log` must print nothing before you trust a run.

Keep every script you ran in `$HANDOFF/repro/`. Write `00-repro.md` with one row per issue:

| Issue | Verdict | Ran in | What was run | What it showed |

- **Verdict:** `confirmed` (it does what the issue says), `not-reproduced` (the steps ran and the behaviour was right), `different` (something nearby is wrong, but not as filed: say what), or `cannot-run` (no script can reach it and a person must look).
- **Ran in:**
  - `app`: the built app with a test project, over MCP. **Only this clears the `unverified` label.** A core-level run, copied code or a stand-in does not.
  - `harness`: the offscreen harness or a probe through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`, running the real `app/Sources` code on a real `.framejob` project, with the real handler reached. This is enough to confirm a key or gesture bug that MCP cannot send, and must be stated as what it is.
  - `probe`: a smaller slice of the code, or the core alone.
  - `reading`: the code only.
- A gesture or a real key press cannot be sent over MCP. Reach the real handler through a probe or the harness. Do not build an instrument that stands in for a person's key press in the live app (root CLAUDE.md): what a real key does is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- Wrong words are confirmed by seeing them in the running app or in `tools/list` (`app`). A source comment has no run, so `reading` plus a test of the behaviour it describes is enough.
- Say what you saw, with the numbers a run printed. Do not write `confirmed` from reading the code. If you could not run it, say `cannot-run`.

**What a verdict means for the batch:**

- `confirmed` by `app` or `harness`: fix it.
- `confirmed` only by `probe`: fix it if the probe reached the code the issue blames, and say so.
- `reading` alone is never a confirmation, except for a source comment or a text string.
- `not-reproduced`: **do not fix it.** The docs pages may still state the filed behaviour, because they were written to match: if so, the page is what's wrong, and the batch corrects it.
- `different`: fix what is actually wrong, if it's in this batch's area. Otherwise it goes under "To file".
- `cannot-run`: no fix, a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, and the issue stays open.

### Owner questions

A decision already in spec §11 is not re-litigated. **A filed behaviour that spec §11 records as deliberate is not a bug:** say so with the ID. A fix that needs a new decision records it in the newest suitable file in `designs/spec/11-decisions/`, with its index row, BEFORE the code. If it needs a genuine owner choice (a trade-off between behaviours, a cost, dropping something they asked for), do not choose:

- If it holds back only some issues, list them in the spec under `## Held for the owner`, each with the question, the options and your recommendation, and go on without them. Their docs pages stay as they are.
- Only if nothing in the batch can proceed, write `STOP: <the question, the options, your recommendation>` at the top of your output.

### Fixes

- **Each fix gets a proof that is red on the base app and green on the fix.** Add rows to the area's proof in `tools/proof/`, or a new script there (`docs_bugs_<batch>_proof.py`), not a throwaway; a core change gets a test in `core/tests/`. Run it against the frozen base app above through `RC_PROOF_APP=<that path>` as well as your build, and record both results. A row that passes on the base proves nothing.
- **Each issue's last line names the docs pages that state today's behaviour.** A fix updates those pages in `docs/site/` (the only user docs since 2026-11-05: `docs/guide/` is retired, and `docs_site_proof.py --guide` fails if it returns), and removes any sentence describing the bug. `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` is the rulebook for the site. Update `docs/site/src/data/features.json` rows it changes. Run `python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py`.
- A user-visible change also follows the root CLAUDE.md's recipe: spec §5.2/§6/§7.9 for anything they mirror, and an MCP mirror for every user-visible edit (handler, catalog entry, comment naming the UI path). The parity check stays clean.
- A persisted field bumps `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` and the header, with a `schema_vN.rs`. The number is provisional until the batch lands; the integrator renumbers if another lane took it.
- A check only a person can make is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, in the same change.
- **File size:** a file at ~600 lines gives something up before it takes anything on, by a pure move committed alone. New files are capped at 400 lines. Frozen files take wiring only. Never run `xcodegen` bare; use `make project`.
- **Residue rule:** a problem the batch uncovers in code it is in is fixed in the batch. Only work that needs the owner, or is as big as the batch, goes under "To file" in your notes, with a draft title and body.
- **Never edit any CLAUDE.md.** List each edit needed under "CLAUDE.md edits owed", with the exact text. The integrator applies them. `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` included.

### Verification

Follows the root CLAUDE.md's "Verification" section.

- Run targeted tests and probes in the loop. `make typecheck` after Swift edits: 0 errors and exactly the 4 baseline warnings. `make lint` after Rust edits.
- `make app-debug` before driving the app. Launch your own instance with `python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch`, and stop only that pid.
- Run mutants for the decisions the batch adds.
- `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete, in the foreground (Bash timeout 600000). Three lanes share the machine, so it can run past the 600 s cap; a re-run skips what already passed, so run it again rather than backgrounding it.
- Run the batch's proof once against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`, after the gate's `make app`).
- Record each command and its result. A number in a record is written only when a run printed it, and a control is called a control.
- Timing is noisy with three lanes running. Repeat a timing-sensitive measurement and say how many runs it took.

### For the adversary and the reviewer

- **Adversary:** treat `00-repro.md` as a claim, not a fact. Read the scripts in `$HANDOFF/repro/`. A row called `confirmed` that didn't run the issue's steps, ran in less than it says, or tested something else is an objection. So is a fix planned for a `not-reproduced` or `reading` row, and a filed behaviour spec §11 records as deliberate.
- **Reviewer:** a fix with no proof row red on the base app is a blocker, and so is a docs page the issue names that still states the old behaviour.

### Commits

The implementer and fixers COMMIT on their worktree's branch, naming paths explicitly, with a plain message. A pure move goes first in its own commit, with a subject starting `Pure move:`. Never commit `FrameJob.xcodeproj`, `tools/proof/work/`, `tools/proof/media/` or build products. Return the base sha (I's HEAD when the worktree started), the tip sha and the worktree path. The integrator turns the range into one commit on I. A commit can take a few minutes to return: the repo's post-commit hook runs `entire`. Wait for it, and don't kill it.

### Things never to do

- **Never open, print, grep or list anything under `.secrets/`.** Never spend money: no `--live` proof, no paid call. The assistant is driven only against its stand-in server.
- **Never run Copy or Cut through the menu**, and never write to the general pasteboard: it overwrites the owner's clipboard. Use a probe that keeps to a private pasteboard, or say `cannot-run`.
- **Never perform a persisting menu item** on any build (View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality).
- **Never take the Mac's focus or put a window in front of the owner.** No `open`, no `osascript`, no System Events, no posted CGEvents.
- **Kill only a pid you launched.** The owner's `/Applications/Frame Job.app` is running and is left alone. So is the docs dev server on port 4321.
- The Concat rule stands: none of its code, shaders, chains or colour tables.

content.text:
# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). - budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:

- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.

  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency

# The owner's answers, 2026-11-06 (binding)

Asked before any batch started, each conditional on the bug being confirmed. A batch whose
confirm stage finds the bug not reproduced does not apply the answer.

| Issue | Question | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #524 | Text, shape and graphic clips have no Crop, Radius or Chroma Key section, but `set_video` and Paste Attributes can still put those values on them. | **Refuse and skip.** `set_video` refuses crop, corner radius and chroma key on these kinds (clearing them stays allowed); Paste Attributes leaves those keys off such a target. |
| #526 | Which spelling do the app's own strings use? | **American.** Matches the Color tab, Key Color, Normalize and macOS. Changes the Document tab's Colour row, the shape tooltips, the "centre" readouts and the Qualifier's "Centre" caption (amends GR-13's caption). Docs prose stays British; pages quote labels as the app spells them. |
| #529, #530 | On a clip with a first-frame cut, should a multi-selection drag and a typed X/Y behave like the single-clip drag (CI-17)? | **Both follow the drag.** Amend CI-13 for the front-most selected clip and CI-2 for typed values on such a clip: the cut and the base move together. |
| #531 | An export over an existing file deletes it once writing starts. | **Write aside, swap.** Write to a temporary file in the same folder and replace the old file only when the export completes. Needs disk room for both files during the export. |
| #521 | The Transcript tab's "Under a transition…" sentence shows by any overlap. | **Reword:** "Near an overlap between two clips: a cut here would leave one clip's tail under the other." The rule itself stays; amends TX-11's sentence; the Delete words page follows. |
| #527 | Follow Speaker: a sounding mic piece with no speech under a shot refuses the whole tool. | **Silent mic, Face if none.** A mic piece with no speech counts as that person not talking in the shot; if no ticked mic has speech there, the shot falls back to Face with the reason. Amends VR-64 (d). |

Each answer that amends a spec §11 decision is recorded there (the decision's file and its index
row) before the code, citing the owner's answer of 2026-11-06.

| #526 | Which spelling do the app's own strings use? | **American.** Matches the Color tab, Key Color, Normalize and macOS. Changes the Document tab's Colour row, the shape tooltips, the "centre" readouts and the Qualifier's "Centre" caption (amends GR-13's caption). Docs prose stays British; pages quote labels as the app spells them. |
| #529, #530 | On a clip with a first-frame cut, should a multi-selection drag and a typed X/Y behave like the single-clip drag (CI-17)? | **Both follow the drag.** Amend CI-13 for the front-most selected clip and CI-2 for typed values on such a clip: the cut and the base move together. |
| #531 | An export over an existing file deletes it once writing starts. | **Write aside, swap.** Write to a temporary file in the same folder and replace the old file only when the export completes. Needs disk room for both files during the export. |
| #521 | The Transcript tab's "Under a transition…" sentence shows by any overlap. | **Reword:** "Near an overlap between two clips: a cut here would leave one clip's tail under the other." The rule itself stays; amends TX-11's sentence; the Delete words page follows. |
| #527 | Follow Speaker: a sounding mic piece with no speech under a shot refuses the whole tool. | **Silent mic, Face if none.** A mic piece with no speech counts as that person not talking in the shot; if no ticked mic has speech there, the shot falls back to Face with the reason. Amends VR-64 (d). |

Each answer that amends a spec §11 decision is recorded there (the decision's file and its index
row) before the code, citing the owner's answer of 2026-11-06.

content.content:
---
title: "The in/out range"
description: Mark a span of the timeline with I and O, so Loop, deletes, exports and other commands work on that passage alone.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The in/out range marks one passage of the timeline. Set it when you want to loop a section, cut it out, export it on its own, or point another command at it.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
  where="Shaded across the timeline's ruler and lanes"
  tools="set_range"
/>

## Set In

Move the playhead to where the passage starts and press <kbd>I</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set In**. With no range yet, the out point goes to the end of the timeline, so the range runs from the playhead to the end.

## Set Out

Move the playhead to where the passage ends and press <kbd>O</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set Out**. With no range yet, the in point goes to the start of the timeline.

<kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> are single-letter keys, so the menu shows no shortcut beside them, and they don't fire while you're typing in a field. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).

## Clear Range

Press <kbd>⌥X</kbd> or choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range**. The item is available only while a range is set.

## What the range is

The range is a span shaded across the ruler and the lanes. It changes nothing by itself. These commands read it:

| Command | What it does with the range |
| --- | --- |
| [Loop](/timeline/loop/) | Plays the range over and over, instead of the whole timeline. |
| <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | With no clip selected, [Lift or Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/) the range. With nothing selected and no range, they beep. |
| [Speed ramp presets](/speed/make-a-ramp/) | Cover the range when it lies entirely inside the clip. |
| [**Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**](/color/adjustment-clips/) | Covers the range. With no range it covers the selected clips, or the whole timeline. |
| [Export](/export/range/) | Writes only the range when you set **Range:** to **In/out range**. |
| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | Changes the speed of everything in the range. |
| [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) | Opens a new project made of the range. |
| [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) | Offers **In/out range** under **From**, which takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole. |
| [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Works over the range. With no range it works over the selected angle clips. |

Two other things set the range for you. Selecting words in the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/) makes them the range, and clearing that selection clears it. **Preview** for a [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) sets the range to the clip and turns Loop on, and both stay until you clear them.

## Crossing points

Setting an in point after the out point moves the out point to match, and setting an out point before the in point moves the in point. Both points then sit on the playhead, which is a range of no length, until you set the other end.

A range of no length isn't shaded, and Loop plays the whole timeline. <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> treat it as no range at all, and the export sheet doesn't offer it. **Mark ▸ Clear Range** still clears it.

## The range isn't saved

The range belongs to the window you're working in, not to the project:

- Setting or clearing it isn't an undo step, and it doesn't mark the project as edited.
- It isn't saved, so a project always opens with no range.
- It clears when you enter or leave a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/), because a nest's time counts from its own start.

## Good to know

- Edits don't move the range. It stays at the same times while the clips under it change. After <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> on a range, the range is still there and now covers what moved up into it, so a second <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> cuts again. Cutting words in the Transcript tab is the exception, and clears the range.
- Inside a nest you can set a range for Loop, deleting and **Retime Range**, but not for an export. The export sheet's **Range:** stays on **Whole project**, and its tooltip explains that the range belongs to the nest. **New Project from Range** is off while a nest is open.

## With an agent

[`set_range`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_range) sets either end or both, and clears the range when called with neither. Given one end, the other keeps its value, or falls back to the start or the end of the project when there's no range yet. Unlike Set In and Set Out, it won't move the other point for you, so an end at or before the start is an error.

[`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/) reports the range as `in_out_range`, and [`export`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#export) with `range` set to `in_out` writes only that span. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

## Related

- [Loop playback](/timeline/loop/)
- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
- [Export a range](/export/range/)
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)

You set it with in and out points. You can't drag a range on the ruler; the timeline only shades the range once it's set.

2. **End:** put the playhead where it ends and press **O** (or **Mark ▸ Set Out**).

- **Setting only one end:** if you set only an In, the range runs to the end of the timeline. If you set only an Out, it starts at the beginning.
- **Crossing points:** setting an In after the Out moves the Out to match, and the reverse.
- **Typing:** **I** and **O** don't fire while you're typing in a field.

**What uses the range:** Loop plays it, Delete or Ripple Delete removes it when no clip is selected, and Export can write only the range. Retime Range, New Project from Range, Generate Captions, adjustment clips and Switch by Speaker also use it.

- **Transcript tab:** selecting words there also sets the range.
- **Not saved:** the range isn't an undo step and isn't saved with the project.
- **Agent:** `set_range` sets it over MCP.

The full page is `docs/site/src/content/docs/timeline/in-out-range.mdx`, which will be at `/timeline/in-out-range/` once the site is published.

content.content: # Doctored Fixing Pixels. Doctored is a native macOS image editor for photographers: a Swift/AppKit app over a Rust core that does the image work. It is free and open source. It was formerly named Rasterize, and it still opens `.rz` documents. ## Download Get the latest notarized build: **[Doctored.dmg](https://github.com/kpgalligan/doctored/releases/latest/download/Doctored.dmg)**. Every release, with its notes, is on the [Releases](https://github.com/kpgalligan/doctored/releases) page. Releases after 0.4.2 update themselves (Doctored ▸ Check for Updates…, and a daily check once you allow it); replace 0.4.1 or 0.4.2 by hand once. Requirements: - An Apple silicon Mac running macOS 15 Sequoia or later. - 16 GB of RAM is the assumed minimum. Smaller Macs get a smaller working limit and may refuse large documents. Doctored ▸ Working Memory… changes the limit. ## What it does - **Layers and masks**: groups, layer masks, vector masks and clipping masks, blend modes, layer styles, fill layers, layer comps, and text and shape layers that stay editable. - **Adjustments and filters**: 22 adjustment-layer types (Levels, Curves, Hue/Saturation, Selective Color…), blur, sharpen and noise filters, Liquify, Lens Correction, and Neural Filters such as Depth Blur that run local models. - **Selections**: marquees, lassos, the magic wand, quick and object selection, Color Range, Select Subject, Sky and people, Select and Mask for hair, Quick Mask, channels and paths. - **Retouching and transforms**: healing, clone stamp, patch, the Remove tool, Content-Aware Fill and Move, dodge and burn, Sky Replacement, Free Transform, Warp and Puppet Warp; Generative Fill and Expand with your own cloud key. - **Camera RAW**: a Develop dialog opens first, and a RAW layer can be re-developed later. CR3, CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG (including ProRAW), RAF and more. - **Colour**: ICC profiles with soft proofing; Bitmap, Grayscale, Duotone, Indexed, RGB, CMYK and Lab modes; 8, 16 and 32-bit float; Merge to HDR. - **Files in and out**: opens PSD and PSB with their layers, TIFF, PNG, JPEG, HEIC, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, OpenEXR and more, and rasterizes PDF and SVG. Save writes the native `.doctored` file. - **Automation and safety**: recordable Actions, Batch, Merge Panorama, Load Files into Stack, Auto-Align and Auto-Blend; auto-recovery, History and snapshots. - **Export and print**: the Export workspace and Quick Export, Export Layers, Contact Sheet, layered PSD, PSB or TIFF at 8, 16 or 32 bits, a one-page PDF, and Print. The full [feature reference](public-docs/src/content/docs/reference/features.md) covers every menu, tool, format and limit. ## AI assistant and agents View ▸ Assistant (⌃⌘A) opens a chat assistant in the right panel that edits the open document, renders the canvas to check its work, and makes each edit one undo step. You bring your own Anthropic API key, entered in the panel's Chat Settings… and stored only on your Mac. External agents connect through the MCP helper bundled in the app. Settings ▸ MCP copies the command that adds it to Claude Code: ```sh claude mcp add --scope user doctored -- '/Applications/Doctored.app/Contents/Helpers/doctored-mcp' ``` An agent can open and render documents and work with layers, selections, painting, filters, adjustments, colour, Actions and export; each edit is one undo step and shows live in the open window. The helper starts Doctored in the background when it is not running and talks to it over a private Unix socket; nothing listens on the network. The [MCP tool reference](public-docs/src/content/docs/reference/mcp-tools.md) lists every tool and its arguments. **Mind the tool count.** The MCP server exposes several hundred tools. A client that loads every tool definition up front spends a large share of its context on them, so an MCP client without a tool search feature (loading definitions on demand) is not practical with Doctored. The tool setup may be reorganized in a future version. Until then, keep this in mind before adding the server globally: the `--scope user` command above makes it available in every session, and leaving out `--scope user` adds it to the current project only. ## Building from source Prerequisites: - Xcode 26 - Rust stable through [rustup](https://rustup.rs) (1.89 or later) - [xcodegen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) (`brew install xcodegen`) - Python 3, for the test and check scripts The first build needs the network for the Rust crates and the Slaude and Sparkle Swift packages. ```sh make app-debug # Debug build → build/Build/Products/Debug/Doctored.app make run # Release build, then launch it make test # the Rust core's test suite make app # Release build → build/Build/Products/Release/Doctored.app ``` Contributor commands and rules are in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). ## Repository layout | Directory | What it holds | | :--- | :--- | | `app/` | The Swift/AppKit app: sources, bridging header, resources, app icon | | `core/` | The Rust staticlib that does the image work, its C header (`include/doctored_core.h`) and its tests | | `agent/` | `doctored-agent`, the assistant's helper (a Swift package on the Slaude Claude API client) | | `mcp-proxy/` | `doctored-mcp`, the stdio MCP helper bundled for external agents | | `scripts/` | The gate, test runners, probes and app drives | | `designs/` | Design decisions (ADRs) and the status docs of open work | | `archive/` | Older design records | | `public-docs/` | Astro/Starlight source for a docs site (not yet published) | | `samples/` | Small generated test images | | `.github/` | The release workflow | ## Contributing Bugs and open work are tracked as [GitHub issues](https://github.com/kpgalligan/doctored/issues). The development rules, for people and coding agents alike, start at [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md), which imports the rules for each side (`core/`, `app/`, `mcp-proxy/` and `agent/`); the docs site has its own `public-docs/CLAUDE.md`. Design decisions live in `designs/` as ADRs, and older records in `archive/` (indexed in `archive/INDEX.md`). History before this repository's first commit, and the measurement harness that wrote the Photoshop test fixtures under `core/tests/fixtures/`, are in the private archive `kpgalligan/doctored-dev`. A fixture folder's README or `photoshop.json` records the run that wrote it. ## Releases Pushing to the `publish` branch builds, signs, notarizes and publishes `Doctored.dmg`, with the signed update feed `appcast.xml` beside it, as a GitHub Release tagged `v.` ([`.github/workflows/publish.yml`](.github/workflows/publish.yml), whose header lists the signing secrets). Local builds are ad-hoc signed and have no updater. ## License Copyright 2026 Kevin Galligan. Doctored is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0; the full text is in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Bundled third-party material keeps its own licence: the fonts are OFL, the Lensfun lens database is CC BY-SA 3.0, the Sparkle update framework is MIT (with the notices in the app's `Acknowledgements.txt`), the assistant's helper is built on [Slaude](https://github.com/kpgalligan/Slaude) (Apache-2.0), a Swift transformation of Anthropic's Python SDK, which is Apache-2.0 with its earlier contributions under MIT (both SDK notices are in `Acknowledgements.txt`), and a downloadable model shows its licence in Settings ▸ Models before it is downloaded. -----INDEX --- title: Documentation description: Documentation for Doctored, a native macOS raster image editor. eyebrow: Documentation template: splash hero: # Distinct from `title` above so the browser tab reads "Documentation | Doctored" # while the hero still opens with the product name. title: Doctored tagline: A native macOS raster image editor for Apple silicon — Swift and AppKit over a Rust core that does the image work. image: file: ../../assets/doctored-1024.png alt: The Doctored app icon actions: - text: Download link: https://github.com/kpgalligan/doctored/releases/latest/download/Doctored.dmg icon: right-arrow - text: Feature reference link: /reference/features/ variant: minimal - text: MCP tool reference link: /reference/mcp-tools/ variant: minimal --- import { Card, CardGrid } from '@astrojs/starlight/components'; Doctored is a free, open-source image editor for photographers. It runs on an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 15 Sequoia or later, and the download is a notarized DMG. Layers and masks, adjustment layers, selections down to hair, healing and content-aware retouching, Camera RAW, colour modes from Bitmap to Lab, and 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents. View ▸ Assistant opens a chat assistant that edits the open document, using your own Anthropic API key. Settings ▸ MCP copies the command that adds the bundled `doctored-mcp` helper to Claude Code. The [MCP tool reference](/reference/mcp-tools/) lists every tool. Apache-2.0. # Doctored

**Fixing Pixels.**

## In one line

Doctored is a free, open-source image editor for photographers, made for the Mac.

## In a paragraph

Doctored is a native macOS image editor for photographers. It covers layers and masks, adjustment layers, precise selections, retouching, Camera RAW and print-ready colour, and it opens your PSD files with their layers intact. It's free, open source under the Apache 2.0 licence, and built for Apple silicon. An optional AI assistant works on the open document using your own API key, and AI agents can drive the editor over MCP.

---

## What Doctored is

Doctored is a raster image editor written for the Mac from the ground up. The interface is Swift and AppKit, so it looks and behaves like a Mac app. The image processing runs in a Rust core. Documents can be 8-bit, 16-bit or 32-bit float, in RGB, CMYK, Lab, Grayscale and the other classic colour modes.

It's for photographers and retouchers who want a full layer-based editor that runs natively on their Mac, with no subscription and no account.

## What you can do with it

- **Work in layers.** Groups, layer masks, vector masks and clipping masks, blend modes, layer styles, fill layers and layer comps. Text and shape layers stay editable.
- **Adjust without damage.** 22 kinds of adjustment layer, including Levels, Curves, Hue/Saturation and Selective Color, plus blur, sharpen and noise filters, Liquify and Lens Correction.
- **Select exactly what you mean.** Marquees, lassos and the magic wand, object and quick selection, Color Range, Select Subject, sky and people selection, and Select and Mask for hair.
- **Retouch.** Healing, clone stamp, patch and the Remove tool, Content-Aware Fill and Move, dodge and burn, Sky Replacement, Free Transform, Warp and Puppet Warp.
- **Develop RAW files.** A Develop dialog opens camera RAW files first (CR3, CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG including ProRAW, RAF and more), and a RAW layer can be developed again later.
- **Manage colour.** ICC profiles with soft proofing, eight colour modes from Bitmap to Lab, and Merge to HDR.
- **Open what you already have.** PSD and PSB with their layers, TIFF, PNG, JPEG, HEIC, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL and OpenEXR. PDF and SVG open as pixels.
- **Automate.** Record Actions and run them in a batch. Merge panoramas, load files into a stack, and auto-align and auto-blend layers.
- **Export and print.** An Export workspace and Quick Export, Export Layers, contact sheets, layered PSD, PSB or TIFF at 8, 16 or 32 bits, PDF, and Print.
- **Keep your work safe.** Auto-recovery, History and snapshots.

## AI, on your terms

Doctored doesn't need AI, and nothing AI-related runs or downloads until you ask for it.

- **Local models.** Neural Filters such as Depth Blur, Super Zoom, JPEG Artifacts Removal and Colorize run on your Mac. Each model downloads only when you choose it, and shows its licence first.
- **Generative Fill and Expand.** These send the selected area to OpenAI, Gemini or fal using your own key. Doctored shows each provider's terms before the first use.
- **The assistant.** A chat panel that edits the open document, checks its own work by rendering the canvas, and makes each change one undo step. It uses your own Anthropic API key, kept only on your Mac.
- **Agents over MCP.** Doctored bundles an MCP helper, so Claude Code and other MCP clients can open documents and work with layers, selections, filters, adjustments and export. Edits show live in the open window, and each one is a single undo step. The helper talks to Doctored over a private socket, and nothing listens on the network.

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple silicon.
- macOS 15 Sequoia or later.
- 16 GB of memory or more is recommended. Doctored works on smaller Macs with a lower working limit, and may refuse very large documents there.

## Download

The download is a notarized disk image: [Doctored.dmg](https://github.com/kpgalligan/doctored/releases/latest/download/Doctored.dmg). Doctored checks for updates and installs them itself.

## Open source

Doctored is free and open source under the Apache License 2.0. The source code, releases and issue tracker are on [GitHub](https://github.com/kpgalligan/doctored).

Doctored was previously called Rasterize, and it still opens Rasterize's `.rz` documents.

It's in my scratch folder, which is temporary, so copy it out or tell me where it should live in the Doctored repo:

- **What Doctored is and who it's for:** a native Mac app with a Rust core, for photographers and retouchers who want a layer-based editor with no subscription or account.
- **What you can do with it:** ten short groups (layers, adjustments, selections, retouching, RAW, colour, file formats, automation, export and print, safety). It's a shortened version of the README's list.

Generative Fill sends the selection to OpenAI, Gemini or fal using your own key. The assistant uses your own Anthropic key. content.content: # Frame Job [![Frame Job in 90 seconds: watch on YouTube](https://img.youtube.com/vi/An7KjPoofzI/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xkkMhgNRQU) A native macOS video editor. Open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. Every edit you make in the window can also be made by an AI agent over MCP, or by the built-in Assistant, and each one is an ordinary undo step. Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or later. There is no account to make: every AI feature runs on your own API key (Anthropic for the Assistant, AssemblyAI for cloud transcription), and everything else works without one. ## Open a movie and start cutting **File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a `.mov` or `.mp4` — or a drop on the Dock icon, or **Open Video…** in the Welcome window — creates an *untitled* project sized and rated to that file, with the file as the first clip on Track 1, ready to cut. A portrait phone clip opens portrait, and a 29.97 fps file stays 29.97. **Save** then writes a `.framejob` package, offered next to the source. ## Features **Projects and media.** Movies, sound and pictures from everything macOS plays, plus WebM and MKV copied in without re-encoding; missing files relinked; Consolidate Media copies footage into the package. → [Projects and media](docs/site/src/content/docs/projects/start-a-project.mdx) **Timeline.** One kind of track that holds any clip; a frame-accurate ruler, filmstrips and waveforms, zoom about the cursor, snapping, markers, an in/out range, track mute, solo, lock, volume, pan, compressor and limiter, clip names and colour labels. → [The timeline and playback](docs/site/src/content/docs/timeline/tracks.mdx) **Editing.** Move, nudge, trim, slip, roll, split, lift, ripple delete, close gap, insert time, insert and overwrite, copy and paste, Paste Attributes, and nests that group clips into one. → [Editing clips](docs/site/src/content/docs/editing/how-edits-work.mdx) **Canvas and layers.** Move, scale, rotate and crop on the preview; opacity, blend modes, shadows, filters, chroma key, spotlight and obscure; Remove Background, which keeps the person (or a photo's subject) and drops the rest with no green screen, found on your Mac, and Text Behind Subject, a title the person stands in front of; text, shape, image and background clips; matte tracks that cut the track behind them. → [Canvas, layers, text and shapes](docs/site/src/content/docs/canvas/the-canvas.mdx) **Vertical and framing.** Faces, people and the regions the eye goes to, found on your Mac and drawn over the preview by View ▸ Show Subjects; Clip ▸ Follow Subject… frames landscape recordings for a vertical or square canvas, easing onto the subject, cutting with the shots and filling the edges with a blurred copy, as ordinary actions in one undo step. File ▸ Make Vertical Version… turns a whole landscape edit into its 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 version in a new project, each full-frame shot following its subject — or, for a wide shot of two to four people with a microphone each, whoever is talking — and titles and pictures-in-picture kept as placed. → [Vertical and framing](docs/site/src/content/docs/framing/what-is-found.mdx) **Motion and transitions.** Actions that ease any property to a new state over a span — Zoom to Region for screencasts — motion presets for entrances, exits and continuous movement, and thirteen transition styles. → [Motion, actions and transitions](docs/site/src/content/docs/motion/actions.mdx) **Speed.** Constant speed or fit to a length, ⌥-drag rate stretch, keep pitch, reverse, freeze frame, and speed ramps — **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** makes a Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Speed Dip or Speed Burst in one step. → [Speed, reverse and freeze frames](docs/site/src/content/docs/speed/overview.mdx) **Audio.** Per-clip volume, drawn as a line on each clip that you drag and ⌥-click to add points, fades in four shapes, ducking for a clip's length or only while its speech plays, voice isolation (Apple's on-device voice model, which also reduces room echo), sixteen voice effects (pitch, robot, telephone, radio, echo, reverbs and more), channel selection, EQ with voice presets, hum removal, noise reduction, a gate for the pauses, a leveller that evens out a speaker who moves on and off the mic, phrase by phrase, and a de-esser, each set from the clip's own loudness, compressor, pan, mono and a true-peak limiter, each of them animated by actions as the volume is; each clip's loudness and true peak in the inspector; Enhance Voice, which sets a voice recording up for speech from its own measurements in one step; Match Audio, which gives clips another clip's loudness and speech tone; and Normalize to a loudness target (−16 LUFS at −1 dBTP by default, turning the limiter on when a clip's peaks need it) or to a peak, which matches clips; a live loudness meter for the mix as it plays; Synchronize Audio lines up a camera and a separate recorder by their sound, drift included. Detach Audio keeps the sound linked to its picture, so J- and L-cuts stay in sync through every edit, and Attach Audio puts it back. → [Audio](docs/site/src/content/docs/audio/how-audio-works.mdx) **Clean-up tools.** Remove Silences cuts dead air by voice or by level; Remove Filler Words cuts the ums and uhs on their own timings. Both preview the cuts and make them as one undo step. → [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](docs/site/src/content/docs/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work.mdx) **Captions.** Import and export SubRip or WebVTT; generate captions on this Mac or with AssemblyAI, as two-line subtitles or word-by-word captions in five styles. Every caption is an ordinary text clip. → [Captions and transcription](docs/site/src/content/docs/captions/how-captions-work.mdx) **Colour grading.** Light and colour controls, three wheels, curves, eight built-in looks and your own `.cube` LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers, Show Ungraded, and waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram scopes. → [Colour grading](docs/site/src/content/docs/color/color-tab.mdx) **HDR and colour management.** iPhone HDR, HDR10, wide gamut and camera log read as what they are; SDR or HDR (HLG) projects; HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, with Show SDR Version to preview the last. → [HDR and colour management](docs/site/src/content/docs/hdr/how-sources-are-read.mdx) **Motion graphics.** Graphic clips drawn every frame by a small JavaScript module: 23 built-ins, browsed by category with a live looping preview in the Graphic dialog: charts, a gauge and timers, screencast keys and window frames, title, quote and logo cards, and social pop-ups; properties as inspector controls, your own modules too, each saved to share as a `.fjgraphic` file with only the fonts and pictures it uses, which Frame Job opens to import into a project. → [Motion graphics](docs/site/src/content/docs/graphics/what-is-a-graphic.mdx) **Several cameras.** Each camera on a track of its own and a program track cut from them; **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** cuts that program from the microphones, showing whoever is talking and the wide while both talk, and **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸** re-picks a shot from another camera in sync, keeping its span and its dissolves, each in one undo step. → [Podcasts and several cameras](docs/site/src/content/docs/multicam/set-up.mdx) **Screen recording.** A display or a window, with system audio, microphone and click rings, at 30 or 60 fps, into a new project or at the playhead; a camera, on its own or beside the screen as a corner talking head; or a microphone-only voice-over. A screen recording's cursor is recorded separately and drawn by Frame Job, so you can resize, smooth or hide it after the fact. **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** zooms a recording in at its clicks and typing and back out after, as ordinary actions you can edit, and **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays** shows the shortcuts you pressed as keycaps. **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** plays the typing faster where nobody speaks. → [Screen recording](docs/site/src/content/docs/recording/recorder-panel.mdx) **Export.** H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), AV1 in MP4 or WebM (10-bit, with HDR, from its own encoder built in, at three speeds; Opus sound in the WebM), VP9 in WebM for every browser (8-bit, or 10-bit with HDR, also built in, with Opus) and with alpha for transparent web video, ProRes 422 and 4444, M4A, WAV and AIFF (16- or 24-bit, with stems: a file per track beside the mix), GIF and animated PNG; loudness targets reached through a true-peak master limiter on every export, presets, an Export Queue that runs while you edit, and single frames as stills. → [Exporting](docs/site/src/content/docs/export/export-sheet.mdx) **The Assistant.** A conversation with Claude in the inspector that edits the open project with the same tools an agent uses, asks before it saves or exports, and shows what each turn cost. → [The Assistant](docs/site/src/content/docs/assistant/set-up.mdx) **The Transcript.** Everything said on the timeline as text in the inspector, in paragraphs with timecodes, read on this Mac or from an AssemblyAI transcript; the spoken word lights up and the text follows it as the video plays, and a click on a word moves the playhead there. Select words and press ⌫ to cut them out of every track at once; click a long pause and press ⌫ to shorten it. → [The Transcript](docs/site/src/content/docs/captions/transcript-tab.mdx) **Agents over MCP.** The whole editor as MCP tools — one per edit plus open, save, render a frame, export and the rest — for Claude Code or any MCP client. → [Driving Frame Job from an AI agent](docs/site/src/content/docs/mcp/overview.mdx) Also: [Settings](docs/site/src/content/docs/reference/settings.mdx), [Menus](docs/site/src/content/docs/reference/menus.mdx) and [keyboard shortcuts](docs/site/src/content/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts.mdx). ## Getting Frame Job The newest signed and notarized build is always at . Open the DMG and drag Frame Job to Applications. An installed copy updates itself (Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…, [Settings](docs/site/src/content/docs/getting-started/updates.mdx)). To build it yourself, see [Developing Frame Job](docs/developing.md). ## Using it with an AI agent Frame Job serves its editor as MCP tools on a local socket only programs you run can open. An MCP client reaches it through `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app, which starts Frame Job in the background on the first tool call if it is not running. **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP ▸ Copy MCP Command** puts the Claude Code registration line on the clipboard, with your copy's path: ```sh claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp' ``` [MCP](docs/site/src/content/docs/mcp/overview.mdx) covers other clients and every tool; [the Assistant](docs/site/src/content/docs/assistant/set-up.mdx) is the same tools inside the window. ## Documentation - [The documentation site](docs/site/README.md) — every feature, a page each. - [The graphics API](docs/graphics-api.md) — writing a graphic module. - [Manual checks](docs/manual-checks.md) — what only a person at the machine can confirm, run before each release. - [The spec](designs/spec/README.md) — the normative design, one file per section. - [Developing Frame Job](docs/developing.md) — building, testing, the architecture and publishing a release. ## Building Xcode 26, Rust, xcodegen and bun; then `make app`. Everything else is in [docs/developing.md](docs/developing.md). ## Languages The GitHub summary makes this look like a Python project, but Python is basically for tests. The app itself if Swift and Rust. | Language | Code | Test | |------------|--------:|--------:| | Swift | 80,760 | 52,303 | | Rust | 22,400 | 54,131 | | Metal | 1,682 | — | | JavaScript | 755 | 2,669 | | TypeScript | 754 | 238 | | Python | 739 | 131,328 | | C header | 144 | 6 | | Shell | 46 | 109 | | **Total** | **107,280** | **240,784** | Non-blank, non-comment lines counted by `cloc` over the tracked files (2026-10-29), vendored third-party code left out. Test is `core/tests`, `graphic/tests`, `mcp-proxy/tests`, the assistant helper's `*.test.ts`, the licence generator's self-test and `tools/proof/` (the proof scripts, probes, offscreen harness and spikes). ## License Frame Job is licensed under the [Apache License, Version 2.0](LICENSE). The bundled fonts and the voice-activity model carry their own licences, beside them in `app/Resources/Fonts/` and `app/Resources/Models/`, and the patched copy of tiny-skia in `graphic/vendor/tiny-skia/` keeps its BSD-3-Clause licence. 0.3

---
title: Documentation
description: A native macOS video editor. Cut, grade, caption, animate and export it yourself, or ask the Assistant or any MCP agent to do it.
eyebrow: Documentation
template: splash
editUrl: false
hero:
  # Distinct from `title` above, so the browser tab reads "Documentation | Frame Job" while the
  # hero opens with the product's name.
  title: Frame Job
  tagline: A native macOS video editor. Cut it yourself, ask the Assistant, or let any MCP agent drive. Every edit is an ordinary undo step.
  image:
    file: ../../assets/logo.svg
    alt: The Frame Job mark, a frame and a playhead inside a viewfinder's four corners
  actions:
    - text: Get started
      link: /getting-started/requirements-and-install/
      variant: primary
      icon: right-arrow
    - text: All features
      link: /features/

---
title: AI features and your own keys
description: Which features need nothing, which use an on-device model, which need your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, and what ever leaves your Mac.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Most of Frame Job needs no key and no network. The few features that send your words or audio to a cloud model run on your own API keys, so you decide what's used and you pay the provider directly.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where={['Settings ▸ Assistant', 'Settings ▸ Transcription']}
  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers']}
  needs="Your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, only for the features that send to them."
/>

## Your own keys

There's no Frame Job account and no relay in between. There are two keys in all, and each provider bills your account directly.

| Key | Turns on | Saved in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | The Assistant | [Settings ▸ Assistant](/assistant/set-up/) |
| AssemblyAI | Cloud captions and Remove Filler Words | [Settings ▸ Transcription](/captions/assemblyai-key/) |

Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each Assistant turn and each month costs. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). The provider's bill is the real figure.

With no key set, Settings says "No API key is set." in its ordinary muted colour. That only means there's no key yet, and it isn't an error.

## What needs what

Anything that sends your words or audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.

| What it takes | Features |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing | Editing, colour, graphics, recording, export, Split at Shot Changes, and connecting an [MCP client](/mcp/overview/#an-mcp-client-or-the-assistant), which brings its own model |
| An on-device model, with no key and no upload | **Generate Captions** with **On this Mac**, Remove Silences' voice analysis, Enhance Voice and Voice Isolation, Remove Background, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and Switch by Speaker |
| Your AssemblyAI key | The **AssemblyAI** engine of **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** with its **Transcribe** buttons |
| Your Anthropic key | The Assistant |

Filler removal works only through AssemblyAI. There's no on-device version.

Without your Anthropic key, **View ▸ Assistant** still opens the tab, which says how to add the key.

Work you've already paid for keeps working with no key:

- **Generate** isn't greyed when every file is already transcribed.
- **Remove Filler Words…** stays on while a file it would work on has a current transcript made with filler words.

An on-device language that isn't installed yet shows a **Download** row in the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet.

## Greyed commands

A command that needs a key you haven't set is greyed rather than hidden, and it says which key and where to set it.

A greyed menu item's title gains the key's name, as in **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. Rest the pointer on a greyed command or button and it reads:

> No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.

For the Assistant it's the same sentence with Anthropic and Assistant. The Assistant tab itself reads "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." with an **Open Settings…** button.

An agent's tool stops with the same sentence, at the point it would send. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what still works without a key.

## Saving a key takes effect at once

Saving or removing a key updates open sheets and menu items straight away. An open Generate Captions sheet turns **Generate** back on with the sheet still up, and there's nothing to reopen or relaunch.

## What stays on this Mac

Editing, analysis, on-device transcription, recording and export all stay on this Mac. Only these reach the network, and each is something you start or can see:

| Goes to | What | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AssemblyAI | The audio of the files being transcribed | When you press **Generate** or **Transcribe** with that engine. **Verify** in Settings also makes a small request with your key, with no audio. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/). |
| Anthropic | Your Assistant messages, the project's details and the frames it renders | While you use the Assistant. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/). |
| GitHub | A request for LiteLLM's published price table, which the cost estimates use, with no key and no project data | At most once a day, from the Assistant's helper |
| GitHub | A check of the update feed, and the update itself when you choose to install one | In the [downloaded copy](/getting-started/updates/) only, when you check or if you allowed automatic checks |
| macOS's own download | An on-device speech model | When you ask for one |

10:Frame Job runs on an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 26 or later. It's free, there's no account to make, and you can start cutting as soon as it's in your Applications folder.
13:  needs={['An Apple Silicon Mac', 'macOS 26 or later']}
20:| An Apple Silicon Mac | Frame Job is built for Apple Silicon alone, so an Intel Mac can't run it. There's no Windows, Linux, iPad or iPhone version. |
21:| macOS 26 or later | 26.0 is the oldest system it opens on. |
48:Frame Job asks you for nothing the first time it opens: no account, no key and no system permission. As with any app downloaded from the internet, macOS may ask you to confirm that you want to open it.

# Frame Job

**A native macOS video editor. Cut it yourself, ask the Assistant, or let any MCP agent drive.**

## In one line

Frame Job is a free, open-source video editor for the Mac, which you, its built-in Assistant or any AI agent can edit with.

## In a paragraph

Frame Job is a native macOS video editor. Open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. It's built for spoken video: you can cut by deleting words from the transcript, take out silences and filler words, record your screen and camera, and turn a landscape edit into a vertical one. Every edit you make in the window can also be made by the built-in Assistant or by an AI agent over MCP, and each one is an ordinary undo step. It's free, open source under the Apache 2.0 licence, and there's no account to make.

---

## What Frame Job is

Frame Job is a video editor written for the Mac from the ground up. The interface is Swift and AppKit, playback and export use Apple's own video frameworks, and the compositing runs on the GPU through Metal. The editing model, every edit and the timeline itself live in a Rust core.

It's for people who make video with a person talking in it: screencasts and tutorials, podcasts, interviews and talking-head clips for social media. It's also a complete general editor, with layered tracks, colour grading, motion graphics and HDR.

## What you can do with it

- **Start in seconds.** Open a `.mov` or `.mp4` and Frame Job makes a project sized and timed to it, with the file already on the timeline. A portrait phone clip opens portrait, and a 29.97 fps file stays 29.97.
- **Edit on tracks that hold anything.** Trim, slip, roll, split, ripple delete, insert and overwrite, and group clips into nests. The timeline has filmstrips and waveforms, snapping, markers, and track mute, solo and lock.
- **Compose on a canvas.** Move, scale, rotate and crop on the preview. Add text, shapes and pictures, blend modes, shadows and chroma key, and use matte tracks to cut one layer with another. Remove Background keeps the person and drops the rest, with no green screen.
- **Animate.** Ease any property to a new state over a span of time, use Zoom to Region for screencasts, pick from motion presets for entrances and exits, and choose from thirteen transition styles.
- **Change speed.** Constant speed or fit to a length, keep pitch, reverse, freeze frames, and speed ramps made in one step.
- **Make the sound right.** Volume lines and fades, ducking under speech, voice isolation, EQ, hum and noise removal, a leveller, a de-esser, compressor and limiter, and sixteen voice effects. Enhance Voice sets a voice recording up in one step, Normalize brings clips to a loudness target, and Synchronize Audio lines a camera up with a separate recorder by their sound.
- **Grade.** Light and colour controls, three wheels, curves, built-in looks and your own `.cube` LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers, and waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram scopes.
- **Work in HDR.** iPhone HDR, HDR10, wide gamut and camera log are read as what they are. Make SDR or HDR projects, and deliver HLG, HDR10 and an SDR version.
- **Add motion graphics.** 23 built-in graphics, including charts, timers, keyboard keys for screencasts, title and quote cards and social pop-ups, each with its own controls. Write your own in JavaScript and share them as a single file.
- **Export.** H.264, HEVC (including 10-bit and transparent video), AV1 and VP9 for the web, ProRes, audio-only files with a separate file per track, GIF and animated PNG. Every export meets its loudness target, and the Export Queue runs while you keep editing.

## Made for spoken video

- **Edit the transcript.** Everything said on the timeline appears as text, and the spoken word lights up as the video plays. Select words and press Delete to cut them from every track at once.
- **Take out the gaps.** Remove Silences cuts dead air, and Remove Filler Words cuts the ums and uhs. You preview the cuts first, and they land as one undo step.
- **Caption.** Generate captions on your Mac or with AssemblyAI, as two-line subtitles or word-by-word captions in five styles, or import and export SubRip and WebVTT.
- **Record your screen.** Record a display or a window with system audio, your microphone and click rings, with your camera in the corner if you like. The cursor is recorded separately, so you can resize, smooth or hide it afterwards. Auto Zoom zooms in on your clicks and typing, and Speed Up Typing plays the typing faster where nobody speaks.
- **Go vertical.** Follow Subject keeps the person in frame on a vertical or square canvas. Make Vertical Version turns a whole landscape edit into 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1, following whoever is talking in a wide shot of several people.
- **Cut a podcast from several cameras.** Switch by Speaker cuts the program from the microphones, showing whoever is talking and the wide shot while both talk.

## AI, on your terms

Most of Frame Job needs no key and no network. There's no Frame Job account and no service in between.

- **On your Mac.** On-device captions, voice detection for Remove Silences, voice isolation, Remove Background, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and Switch by Speaker all run locally, with no key and no upload.
- **Your own keys.** The two features that send audio or words to a cloud model use your own API keys, and the provider bills you directly: AssemblyAI for cloud captions and filler words, and Anthropic for the Assistant. A feature that needs a key you haven't set says which key and where to set it.
- **The Assistant.** A conversation with Claude in the inspector that edits the open project with the same tools an agent uses. It asks before it saves or exports, and shows what each turn cost.
- **Agents over MCP.** The whole editor is available as MCP tools: one per edit, plus open, save, render a frame and export. Claude Code or any other MCP client can drive it. Settings copies the command that connects Claude Code. The connection is a local socket that only programs on your Mac can open, and Frame Job starts in the background when an agent first needs it.

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple silicon.
- macOS 26 or later.

## Download

The download is a signed and notarized disk image: [FrameJob.dmg](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/FrameJob.dmg). Open it and drag Frame Job to Applications. Frame Job updates itself, through **Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…** or automatic checks if you allow them.

## Open source

Frame Job is free and open source under the Apache License 2.0. The source code, releases and issue tracker are on [GitHub](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob).

## In one line

Frame Job is a free, open-source video editor for the Mac, which you, its built-in Assistant or any AI agent can edit with.
